title: Python SDK: typed response schemas, pydantic/dataclass models & streaming helpers
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: The Python SDK currently returns loosely typed dicts for generation and streaming APIs which makes end-user code verbose and error-prone. Goal: deliver first-class typed models and structured-output helpers that work with both synchronous and streaming responses, and offer a minimal runtime dependency surface (option to use pydantic or stdlib dataclasses).

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Provide canonical response schemas for text generation, chat messages, embeddings, and tool/function call frames as typed Python objects.
- Two model implementations: pydantic v2 models (default for validation and parsing) and lightweight dataclasses/frozen types for users who avoid pydantic.
- Streaming ergonomics: typed incremental events (TokenEvent, DeltaEvent, FinalResponse) with an iterator/async iterator API that yields typed objects rather than raw JSON chunks.
- Structured output helpers: convenience parsers for JSONL/JSON-in-text outputs, robust parse-with-retry, and hooks for post-validation and regeneration suggestions.
- Backwards compatibility: keep existing dict-based return modes via optional parameter (raw=True) and provide migrations guide in docs.
- Tests: unit parsing tests, fuzz tests for partial stream chunks, and integration tests against the sandbox hosted endpoint.

Design decisions so far:
- Default to pydantic v2 for runtime validation and helpful errors; expose a factory to build dataclass-backed models for low-dep environments.
- Use schema versioning ("schema_version" on model meta) to enable safe rollouts and server-driven feature flags.
- Streaming parser will buffer until a complete logical event is available and expose a forgiving mode for partial JSON tokens with best-effort assembly.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Pydantic v2 introduces an additional dependency; should we vendor a tiny validation helper for extremely minimal installs? (PM prefers explicit opt-in for dataclasses.)
- How to represent function/tool calls with both argument schemas and freeform args (union typing or typed wrapper)?

Deliverables:
- SDK API: SDKClient.generate(..., response_model=ResponseModel, stream=True/False) and convenience methods: .as_typed(), .stream_tokens(as_type=TokenEvent).
- Migration doc + code snippets for common patterns (chat turn extraction, structured JSON output parsing, streaming token transforms).
- Example notebook and three short examples in examples/python/ showing pydantic models, dataclass models, and streaming consumer that writes to a typed event log.
